precision.name: North Station
precision.text:
# Harbour Station monthly report, May 2025

The station's only pump, KV12-0457, tripped three times in the first week of May on low suction pressure. On 6 May Rosa Delgado found the intake screen half blocked with leaves and cleaned it. No trip has occurred since.

Average flow for the month was 17 litres per second. The station was unmanned for the rest of May, with alarms routed to North Station.

precision.name: experiments
precision.text:
# Institute Newsletter, Spring 2025

## Field-work award

Maria Lopez of the Soil Ecology team received this year's Hensley Field-Work Award for her peat sampling campaign on the Aldmoor bog, where she collected 240 cores over two winters. Her group leader, Dr. Jonathan Pike, called the campaign "the most complete record of the bog we have".

## New hydrology flume

The Hydrology team, led by research engineer Aiko Tanaka, has finished building a 12-metre sediment flume in the basement laboratory. The first experiments start in May.

precision.name: group leader
precision.text:
# Finance Office memo: travel claims

From: Maria Lopez, grants accountant

Travel claims for May must reach the Finance Office by 15 June 2025; later claims are paid in August. Please attach every receipt.

Several colleagues have asked how the June conference trips are funded. The trip of Maria Lopez (Soil Ecology) to the peat conference in Utrecht is charged to the Aldmoor peat project, as agreed with her group leader.

precision.name: bakery
precision.text:
# New bakery on Harbour Street

Maria Lopez has opened a bakery at 14 Harbour Street, in the former post office. She trained in Valencia and bakes rye bread and pastries every morning from five.

"The street is full of potholes," she said. "I hope the resurfacing starts before winter, or my customers will stop coming."

precision.name: rain
precision.text:
# Public meeting on Station Road flooding

About eighty residents came to the town hall on Thursday to discuss the flooding of Station Road.

Dr Jonathan Pike of the environmental institute explained how the peat bogs upstream hold back rain and slow the flow into the river. The council's structural inspector, Daniel Okafor, said the culvert under Station Road is too narrow for heavy storms.

Mayor Helen Achterberg said the drainage works will start in September. Councillor Priya Nandakumar repeated her call to move them ahead of the Harbour Street resurfacing.

precision.name: residents
precision.text:
# Council votes on two repairs

The Riverton town council voted 7 to 2 on Tuesday to repair the Mill Lane footbridge and to replace the roof of the Eastgate library.

The footbridge will be closed from 3 February while its railings and deck boards are renewed. The library roof, which has leaked into the children's section since the autumn storms, will be replaced over the summer, when the library closes for four weeks.

Mayor Helen Achterberg said the footbridge "is safe to use until the works begin". The council's structural inspector, Daniel Okafor, wrote in his report that residents had told him the east railing moved when leaned on; he recommended closing the bridge at once.

# Minutes of the institute committee, 9 June 2025

Present: Aiko Tanaka (chair), Maria Lopez (Finance Office), J. Pike, Samuel Osei.

1. Aldmoor overrun. J. Pike explained the equipment overrun of the Aldmoor peat project: a second corer had to be bought after the first one jammed in December. The committee accepted the explanation.

2. Flume. Samuel Osei measured the flume pump vibration at 60 litres per second: 2.3 mm/s, below the 4.5 mm/s limit. Experiments above 60 litres per second may now start.

precision.name: peat as a carbon archive
precision.text:
# Back from Utrecht

Two of our researchers attended the European peat conference in Utrecht in June 2025. Maria Lopez presented a poster on the 240 cores of the Aldmoor bog, which drew more questions than any other poster in her session. Dr. Jonathan Pike chaired the session on peat as a carbon archive.

Next year's conference will be held in Tartu.

precision.text:
# Incident report: flooding of the North Station dry well

On 29 March 2025 the mechanical seal of pump HP40-1183 failed during the night shift. About 3,000 litres of water flooded the dry well before the operator isolated the pump. Flow on the North main dropped to 31 litres per second until HP40-2291 was switched to duty.

Site engineer Tomasz Wren wrote that the flooding would have been avoided had the seal been replaced after the March inspection, as the inspection had recommended.

The seal of HP40-1183 was replaced on 31 March 2025 by technician Rosa Delgado.

precision.text:
## Contents

1. Before you start
2. Isolating a duty pump

# Isolating a pump at North Station

Written by Tomasz Wren for new operators.

## Before you start

Tell the control room which pump you will isolate, and check that the standby pump is available.

## Isolating a duty pump

Switch the standby pump to duty first. Then stop the pump you are isolating, close its discharge valve, and close its suction valve last. Lock both valves and hang a tag on the starter.

precision.text:
# North Station pump inspection, 14 March 2025

Technician Rosa Delgado inspected both Hydra P-40 pumps at North Station during the quarterly round.

Pump HP40-1183 showed a slow drip from the mechanical seal and a bearing temperature of 71 °C, above the 65 °C alarm limit. Delgado tagged it for a seal replacement within two weeks.

Pump HP40-2291 ran quietly. No leaks were found on HP40-2291, and its bearing temperature was 48 °C.

Measured flow: HP40-1183 delivered 38 litres per second, HP40-2291 delivered 41 litres per second.

precision.name: chair
precision.text:
# Minutes of the institute committee, 9 June 2025

Present: Aiko Tanaka (chair), Maria Lopez (Finance Office), J. Pike, Samuel Osei.

1. Aldmoor overrun. J. Pike explained the equipment overrun of the Aldmoor peat project: a second corer had to be bought after the first one jammed in December. The committee accepted the explanation.

2. Flume. Samuel Osei measured the flume pump vibration at 60 litres per second: 2.3 mm/s, below the 4.5 mm/s limit. Experiments above 60 litres per second may now start.

3. Travel. Maria Lopez reported that 60 percent of the 2025 travel budget has been spent.

Aiko Tanaka closed the meeting at 15:55.

The Eastgate library reopened on 1 September with its new roof. The contractor finished on 25 August, a week ahead of the deadline.

1. Budget. Maria Lopez presented the grants budget for 2025-26. The Aldmoor peat project is 18,000 euros over its equipment line; she asked the project lead to explain the overrun by the next meeting.

# Public meeting on Station Road flooding

About eighty residents came to the town hall on Thursday to discuss the flooding of Station Road.

Dr Jonathan Pike of the environmental institute explained how the peat bogs upstream hold back rain and slow the flow into the river. The council's structural inspector, Daniel Okafor, said the culvert under Station Road is too narrow for heavy storms.

Mayor Helen Achterberg said the drainage works will start in September. Councillor Priya Nandakumar repeated her call to move them ahead of the Harbour Street resurfacing.

precision.text:
# Institute Newsletter, Spring 2025

## Field-work award

Maria Lopez of the Soil Ecology team received this year's Hensley Field-Work Award for her peat sampling campaign on the Aldmoor bog, where she collected 240 cores over two winters. Her group leader, Dr. Jonathan Pike, called the campaign "the most complete record of the bog we have".

## New hydrology flume

The Hydrology team, led by research engineer Aiko Tanaka, has finished building a 12-metre sediment flume in the basement laboratory. The first experiments start in May.

# Harbour Station monthly report, May 2025

The station's only pump, KV12-0457, tripped three times in the first week of May on low suction pressure. On 6 May Rosa Delgado found the intake screen half blocked with leaves and cleaned it. No trip has occurred since.

Average flow for the month was 17 litres per second. The station was unmanned for the rest of May, with alarms routed to North Station.

## Contents

# Isolating a pump at North Station

Written by Tomasz Wren for new operators.

## Before you start

Tell the control room which pump you will isolate, and check that the standby pump is available.

## Isolating a duty pump

Switch the standby pump to duty first. Then stop the pump you are isolating, close its discharge valve, and close its suction valve last. Lock both valves and hang a tag on the starter.

precision.text:
# North Station: summary of 2024

North Station pumped 1.9 million cubic metres in 2024. HP40-1183 ran for 6,100 hours and HP40-2291 for 2,300 hours, as HP40-1183 was kept on duty for most of the year.

No seal failures were recorded in 2024. The only stoppage was a four-hour power cut on 17 November, when both pumps were off.

For 2025 the site engineer, Tomasz Wren, plans to share the duty more evenly between the two pumps.
